es.R: Morirán de hambre, y enfermedades terribles acabarán con ellos. \q Les enviaré animales salvajes que los muerdan \q y serpientes venenosas que los piquen.

fr.L: [Ils seront] épuisés par la faim, dévorés par la peste et une destruction amère ; \q et la dent des bêtes, je l’enverrai contre eux, \q avec le venin de ce qui rampe dans la poussière.
fr.B: Ils dépériront de faim, dévorés par la fièvre et par un mal mortel. \q J’enverrai contre eux les crocs des bêtes sauvages \q et le venin des serpents qui glissent dans la poussière.
fr.R: Ils mourront de faim, et de terribles maladies les détruiront. \q J’enverrai des bêtes sauvages pour les mordre \q et des serpents venimeux pour les piquer.

sw.L: [Watadhoofishwa] na njaa, wataliwa na tauni na maangamizi machungu; \q na meno ya wanyama nitayatuma juu yao, \q pamoja na sumu ya viumbe vinavyotambaa katika vumbi.
sw.B: Watadhoofika kwa njaa, wataangamizwa na homa na ugonjwa wa kufisha. \q Nitatuma dhidi yao meno ya wanyama wakali \q na sumu ya nyoka wanaoteleza mavumbini.
sw.R: Watakufa kwa njaa, na magonjwa mabaya yatawaangamiza. \q Nitatuma wanyama wakali wawaume \q na nyoka wenye sumu wawagonge.

decisions.choice: plague: burning fever or pestilence
decisions.reason: The word means a flame or a fiery disease. It is also the name of a Canaanite god of plague; Habakkuk 3:5 pictures plague going out before God as his servant.

decisions.choice: bitter destruction: deadly disease
decisions.reason: The word means a destroying sting or pestilence (Psalm 91:6; Isaiah 28:2).

decisions.choice: things crawling in the dust: snakes
decisions.reason: The phrase describes snakes (Micah 7:17; Genesis 3:14).

decisions.choice: hunger, plague and beasts: the punishments of the covenant
decisions.reason: The same troubles are named as covenant curses in Leviticus 26:22, 25-26 and Deuteronomy 28:21-22.

decisions.choice: wild animals to bite them, poisonous snakes to strike them
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what the teeth and venom are.

source.text: מִחוּץ֙ תְּשַׁכֶּל־חֶ֔רֶב וּמֵחֲדָרִ֖ים אֵימָ֑ה גַּם־בָּחוּר֙ גַּם־בְּתוּלָ֔ה יוֹנֵ֖ק עִם־אִ֥ישׁ שֵׂיבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: From outside will bereave a sword, and from inner rooms terror, both young man and young woman, nursing child with man of gray hair.

en.L: Outside the sword will bereave, \q and in the inner rooms [will be] terror, \q both young man and young woman, \q the nursing child with the man of gray hair.
en.B: In the streets the sword will take their children, \q and inside their homes terror will strike, \q young men and young women alike, \q the nursing baby and the gray-haired.
en.R: Outside, people will be killed in battle. \q Inside their houses, people will be terrified. \q Young men and young women will die, \q and so will babies and old people.

es.L: Fuera, la espada arrebatará los hijos, \q y en los cuartos interiores [reinará] el terror, \q lo mismo al muchacho que a la muchacha, \q al que mama junto con el anciano canoso.
es.B: En las calles la espada les quitará los hijos, \q y dentro de las casas golpeará el terror, \q a jóvenes y doncellas por igual, \q al bebé de pecho y al de cabellos blancos.
es.R: Afuera, la gente morirá en la guerra. \q Dentro de sus casas, la gente estará aterrada. \q Morirán los jóvenes y las jóvenes, \q y también los bebés y los ancianos.

fr.L: Au-dehors l’épée privera d’enfants, \q et dans les chambres [ce sera] la terreur, \q tant le jeune homme que la jeune fille, \q le nourrisson avec l’homme aux cheveux blancs.
fr.B: Dans les rues, l’épée leur arrachera leurs enfants, \q et dans les maisons, la terreur frappera, \q jeunes gens et jeunes filles ensemble, \q le bébé au sein comme le vieillard aux cheveux gris.
fr.R: Dehors, les gens seront tués à la guerre. \q Dans leurs maisons, ils seront terrifiés. \q Les jeunes gens et les jeunes filles mourront, \q et aussi les bébés et les vieillards.

sw.L: Nje upanga utawaondolea watoto, \q na ndani ya vyumba [kutakuwa na] kitisho, \q kijana wa kiume na msichana pia, \q mtoto mchanga pamoja na mzee mwenye mvi.

decisions.choice: the sword will bereave: war will kill their children
decisions.reason: The verb means to make childless (Leviticus 26:22; Lamentations 1:20).

decisions.choice: outside and in the inner rooms: everywhere
decisions.reason: There will be no safe place: the sword in the streets and terror in the most private rooms of the house.

decisions.choice: young man and young woman, infant and gray-haired: everyone, of every age
decisions.reason: Pairing opposites names the whole population.

decisions.choice: will die
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sword will do to each group.

source.text: אָמַ֖רְתִּי אַפְאֵיהֶ֑ם אַשְׁבִּ֥יתָה מֵאֱנ֖וֹשׁ זִכְרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I said, I will cut them in pieces; I will make cease from humankind their memory,

en.L: I said, "I will cut them in pieces; \q I will make their memory cease from humankind,"
en.B: I would have said, "I will scatter them \q and wipe out their memory from among humankind,"
en.R: I would have said, "I will scatter them far away. \q I will make sure no one remembers them."

es.L: Dije: ‘Los haré pedazos; \q haré cesar su recuerdo de entre la humanidad’,
es.B: Habría dicho: ‘Los dispersaré \q y borraré su recuerdo de entre los seres humanos’,
es.R: Habría dicho: ‘Los dispersaré lejos. \q Haré que nadie se acuerde de ellos’,

decisions.choice: I said: I would have said, I would have decided
decisions.reason: God tells what he would have done, but verse 27 says why he held back.

decisions.choice: cut them in pieces: destroy them completely, perhaps by scattering them
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here. It may come from the word for a corner or edge, "I will drive them into the corners"; the Greek translation has "I will scatter them".

decisions.choice: make their memory cease: wipe them out so that no one remembers them
decisions.reason: The same is said of Amalek (25:19; Exodus 17:14).

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for God's words to himself inside his speech
decisions.reason: God's speech is already in single quotes inside Moses' song, so words he quotes take double quotes.

source.text: לוּלֵ֗י כַּ֤עַס אוֹיֵב֙ אָג֔וּר פֶּֽן־יְנַכְּר֖וּ צָרֵ֑ימוֹ פֶּן־יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ יָדֵ֣ינוּ רָ֔מָה וְלֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה פָּעַ֥ל כָּל־זֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: if not [the] provocation of an enemy I dreaded, lest misconstrue their adversaries, lest they say, Our hand [is] raised, and not Yahweh did all this.

en.L: had I not feared the provocation of the enemy, \q lest their adversaries misunderstand, \q lest they say, "Our hand [is] raised high, \q and [it was] not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [who] did all this."'
en.B: but I feared the taunting of the enemy, \q that their foes would misunderstand \q and say, "Our own power has won; \q it was not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who did all this."'
en.R: But I did not want their enemies to boast. \q I did not want them to misunderstand and say, \q "We won by our own strength. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did not do this."'

es.L: si no hubiera temido la provocación del enemigo, \q no fuera que sus adversarios lo malinterpretaran, \q no fuera que dijeran: ‘Nuestra mano [está] en alto, \q y no [fue] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [quien] hizo todo esto’”.
es.B: pero temí las burlas del enemigo, \q que sus adversarios se equivocaran \q y dijeran: ‘Nuestro propio poder ha vencido; \q no fue {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien hizo todo esto’”.
es.R: Pero no quería que sus enemigos se jactaran. \q No quería que se equivocaran y dijeran: \q ‘Ganamos con nuestras propias fuerzas. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hizo esto’”.

fr.L: si je n’avais craint la provocation de l’ennemi, \q de peur que leurs adversaires ne se méprennent, \q de peur qu’ils ne disent : ‘Notre main [est] levée bien haut, \q et ce n’[est] pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [qui] a fait tout cela.’”
fr.B: mais j’ai craint les sarcasmes de l’ennemi : \q leurs adversaires se seraient mépris \q et auraient dit : ‘C’est notre propre force qui a vaincu ; \q ce n’est pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui a fait tout cela.’”
fr.R: Mais je ne voulais pas que leurs ennemis s’en vantent. \q Je ne voulais pas qu’ils se trompent et disent : \q ‘Nous avons gagné par notre propre force. \q Ce n’est pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui a fait cela.’”

sw.L: kama nisingaliogopa uchokozi wa adui, \q wasije watesi wao wakaelewa vibaya, \q wasije wakasema, "Mkono wetu [umeinuliwa] juu, \q wala si {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [aliyefanya] haya yote."'
sw.B: lakini niliogopa dhihaka ya adui, \q kwamba watesi wao wangeelewa vibaya \q na kusema, "Nguvu zetu wenyewe zimeshinda; \q si {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyefanya haya yote."'
sw.R: Lakini sikutaka adui zao wajivune. \q Sikutaka waelewe vibaya na kusema, \q "Tumeshinda kwa nguvu zetu wenyewe. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakufanya jambo hili."'

decisions.choice: the provocation of the enemy: the enemy's taunting that would provoke God
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Israel provoking God in verses 16, 19 and 21; now it is what the enemy would do.

decisions.choice: our hand is raised high: we won by our own power
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a picture of strength and victory (Exodus 14:8; Numbers 33:3; Micah 5:8).

decisions.choice: God's concern that the nations see his hand
decisions.reason: Moses pleaded the same way, that the nations would misread God's acts (9:28; Exodus 32:12; Numbers 14:13-16). God holds back for his own name's sake.

decisions.choice: misunderstand: misread who did it
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as foreign, to misconstrue; the enemies would take the credit.

decisions.choice: the single quotation mark closes God's speech here
decisions.reason: God's words that began in verse 20 end with this verse. Who speaks in verses 28-33 is open (see verse 28).

source.text: כִּי־ג֛וֹי אֹבַ֥ד עֵצ֖וֹת הֵ֑מָּה וְאֵ֥ין בָּהֶ֖ם תְּבוּנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For a nation lost of counsels [are] they, and there is not in them understanding.

en.L: For they [are] a nation lost of counsel, \q and [there is] no understanding in them.
en.B: For they are a nation without sense, \q and there is no understanding in them.
en.R: Those enemies are a nation with no sense. \q They do not understand anything.

decisions.choice: they: the enemy nation of verse 27
decisions.reason: Verses 28-33 most likely describe Israel's enemies, who would claim the victory as their own (verse 27) and whose "rock" and "vine" are not like Israel's (verses 31-32). They can also be read as describing Israel, the "foolish people" of verse 6 who would not see why they were defeated.

decisions.choice: lost of counsel: without good judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase means a people whose plans and sense have perished.

decisions.choice: the speaker is Moses again
decisions.reason: God's own words end at verse 27; "our Rock" in verse 31 shows that the singer is speaking for Israel. God speaks again in verses 34-35.

decisions.choice: those enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant, following the meaning decision.

source.text: ל֥וּ חָכְמ֖וּ יַשְׂכִּ֣ילוּ זֹ֑את יָבִ֖ינוּ לְאַחֲרִיתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: If they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their end.

en.L: If they were wise, they would understand this; \q they would discern their end.
en.B: If only they were wise, they would understand this \q and see what their end will be.
en.R: If only they were wise, they would understand this. \q They would see what is going to happen to them.

decisions.choice: if only: a wish that cannot come true
decisions.reason: The word introduces a condition contrary to fact: they are not wise.

decisions.choice: their end: what will finally become of them
decisions.reason: The word is the one God used in verse 20 ("I will see what their end will be").

source.text: אֵיכָ֞ה יִרְדֹּ֤ף אֶחָד֙ אֶ֔לֶף וּשְׁנַ֖יִם יָנִ֣יסוּ רְבָבָ֑ה אִם־לֹא֙ כִּי־צוּרָ֣ם מְכָרָ֔ם וַֽיהוָ֖ה הִסְגִּירָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: How could pursue one a thousand, and two put to flight ten thousand, unless that their Rock had sold them, and Yahweh had handed them over?

en.L: How could one pursue a thousand, \q and two put ten thousand to flight, \q unless their Rock had sold them, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had handed them over?
en.B: How could one chase a thousand, \q or two drive ten thousand away, \q unless their Rock had sold them, \q unless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had surrendered them?
en.R: How could one enemy soldier chase a thousand Israelites? \q How could two make ten thousand run away? \q It could happen only because their Rock had sold them, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had handed them over.

decisions.choice: their Rock had sold them: Israel's own God gave them up
decisions.reason: "Their Rock" is Israel's God. A defeat so lopsided can only mean that God handed his people over. It turns around the promise that five of Israel would chase a hundred (Leviticus 26:8; Joshua 23:10).

decisions.choice: sold them: handed them over to their enemies
decisions.reason: The same picture is used in Judges 2:14; 3:8; 4:2.

decisions.choice: one enemy soldier, a thousand Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable says who chases whom, following the decision at verse 28.

decisions.choice: Rock, with a capital letter
decisions.reason: "Their Rock" here is Israel's God.

source.text: כִּ֛י לֹ֥א כְצוּרֵ֖נוּ צוּרָ֑ם וְאֹיְבֵ֖ינוּ פְּלִילִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For not like our Rock [is] their rock, and our enemies [are] judges.

en.L: For their rock [is] not like our Rock, \q and our enemies [are] judges [of it].
en.B: For their rock is not like our Rock, \q as even our enemies must admit.
en.R: The enemies' god is not like our Rock. \q Even our enemies know that.

decisions.choice: their rock: the god of the enemies
decisions.reason: The song calls the enemies' god a "rock" to set it against the true Rock (verse 37).

decisions.choice: judges: the enemies themselves can judge that it is so
decisions.reason: The word means those who decide a case. The Greek translation reads "our enemies are without understanding"; some take the line as "our enemies are fools". The sense of the Hebrew seems to be that even the enemies must concede it.

decisions.choice: our: the singer speaks for Israel
decisions.reason: This shows that the voice in these verses is Moses, speaking with his people.

decisions.choice: rock, without a capital letter, for the enemies' god
decisions.reason: Only Israel's God is written "Rock" (see verse 4). Readable says "god" for the enemies' rock.

source.text: כִּֽי־מִגֶּ֤פֶן סְדֹם֙ גַּפְנָ֔ם וּמִשַּׁדְמֹ֖ת עֲמֹרָ֑ה עֲנָבֵ֨מוֹ֙ עִנְּבֵי־ר֔וֹשׁ אַשְׁכְּלֹ֥ת מְרֹרֹ֖ת לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For from [the] vine of Sodom [is] their vine, and from [the] fields of Gomorrah; their grapes [are] grapes of poison; clusters of bitterness [belong] to them.

en.L: For their vine [is] from the vine of Sodom \q and from the fields of Gomorrah; \q their grapes [are] grapes of poison; \q bitter clusters [are] theirs.
en.B: For their vine springs from the vine of Sodom, \q from the fields of Gomorrah. \q Their grapes are grapes of poison, \q and their clusters are bitter.
en.R: They are like a vine that grows in Sodom, \q in the fields of Gomorrah. \q Their grapes are full of poison, \q and their bunches of grapes are bitter.

decisions.choice: Sodom and Gomorrah: cities known for wickedness and destroyed by God
decisions.reason: The two cities stand for corruption that brings ruin (29:22; Genesis 19; Isaiah 1:10).

decisions.choice: vine and grapes: what a people produces, its deeds
decisions.reason: A people is pictured as a vine and its conduct as fruit (Isaiah 5:1-7; Jeremiah 2:21).

decisions.choice: poison: a bitter, poisonous plant
decisions.reason: The word names a poisonous plant and its poison (29:17; Hosea 10:4).

decisions.choice: their: the enemies of verse 31
decisions.reason: As in verse 28, the verse may also describe Israel.

source.text: חֲמַ֥ת תַּנִּינִ֖ם יֵינָ֑ם וְרֹ֥אשׁ פְּתָנִ֖ים אַכְזָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] venom of serpents [is] their wine, and [the] poison of cobras, cruel.

en.L: Their wine [is] the venom of serpents, \q and the cruel poison of cobras.
en.B: Their wine is snake venom, \q the deadly poison of cobras.
en.R: Their wine is like snake poison, \q the deadly poison of cobras.

decisions.choice: serpents: snakes
decisions.reason: The word can mean a great sea creature, but here, as in Exodus 7:9-12 and Psalm 91:13, it means snakes.

decisions.choice: cobras: a deadly kind of snake
decisions.reason: The word names a poisonous snake, perhaps the cobra (Isaiah 11:8; Psalm 58:5).

decisions.choice: their wine: what their vine produces
decisions.reason: Continuing the picture of verse 32, their deeds yield only death.

source.text: הֲלֹא־ה֖וּא כָּמֻ֣ס עִמָּדִ֑י חָתֻ֖ם בְּאוֹצְרֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: ? Not this [is] stored up with me, sealed up in my treasuries?

en.L: '[Is] this not stored up with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q sealed up in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} storehouses?
en.B: 'Is this not laid up in store with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q sealed in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} treasuries?
en.R: 'I have stored this away. \q It is sealed up in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} storerooms.

decisions.choice: God speaks again
decisions.reason: The words "with me" and "my storehouses" show that God is speaking, though the song does not introduce him. His words run through verse 35.

decisions.choice: this is stored up: their deeds and the judgment due for them are kept until the time comes
decisions.reason: God has kept account of what they have done, as something sealed and stored (Job 14:17; Hosea 13:12). Verse 35 says what it is stored for.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for verses 34-35
decisions.reason: These are God's words inside Moses' song.

decisions.choice: a statement for the question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes".

source.text: לִ֤י נָקָם֙ וְשִׁלֵּ֔ם לְעֵ֖ת תָּמ֣וּט רַגְלָ֑ם כִּ֤י קָרוֹב֙ י֣וֹם אֵידָ֔ם וְחָ֖שׁ עֲתִדֹ֥ת לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: To me [belong] vengeance and recompense, for [the] time [when] slips their foot; for near [is the] day of their disaster, and hurries [what is] prepared for them.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [belong] vengeance and repayment, \q for the time when their foot slips; \q for the day of their disaster [is] near, \q and what is prepared for them hurries [on].'
en.B: Vengeance is {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and repayment, \q for the time when their foot slips; \q for the day of their disaster is near, \q and their doom is rushing toward them.'
en.R: I will punish them and pay them back \q when the time comes for them to fall. \q The day of their disaster is coming soon. \q Their doom is rushing toward them.'

decisions.choice: to me belong vengeance and repayment
alternatives: on the day of vengeance and repayment
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "to me". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation read the same letters as "for the day of vengeance" ("on the day of vengeance I will repay"). Romans 12:19 and Hebrews 10:30 quote the line as "Vengeance is mine; I will repay". Reviewers check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: vengeance: just punishment from the judge who sets wrongs right
decisions.reason: The word is not spite but the act of a ruler who punishes wrong and defends those wronged (verses 41, 43).

decisions.choice: their foot slips: they fall into ruin
decisions.reason: A slipping foot is a picture of sudden downfall (Psalm 38:17; 94:18).

decisions.choice: what is prepared for them: the doom that awaits them
decisions.reason: The word means things that are ready, the future that is in store.

decisions.choice: the single quotation mark closes God's words
decisions.reason: Verse 36 speaks of the LORD in the third person, so the singer is speaking again.

source.text: כִּֽי־יָדִ֤ין יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ וְעַל־עֲבָדָ֖יו יִתְנֶחָ֑ם כִּ֤י יִרְאֶה֙ כִּי־אָ֣זְלַת יָ֔ד וְאֶ֖פֶס עָצ֥וּר וְעָזֽוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: For will judge Yahweh his people, and on his servants he will have compassion, when he sees that gone [is] strength, and there is none, shut up or left free.

en.L: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will judge {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people \q and have compassion on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees that [their] strength is gone, \q and [there is] none [left], bound or free.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do justice for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people \q and take pity on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, \q once {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees their strength is spent \q and no one is left, bound or free.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will defend {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. \q He will show mercy to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees that they have no strength left \q and that no one at all remains.

decisions.choice: judge: do justice for, defend the cause of
decisions.reason: Here judging means taking his people's side and setting things right (Psalm 135:14, which repeats this line; Genesis 30:6). Hebrews 10:30 quotes the line as a warning that God will judge his people.

decisions.choice: have compassion: change his course toward them in pity
decisions.reason: The verb means to be moved to pity and so to relent.

decisions.choice: their strength is gone, none left, bound or free: they are utterly helpless
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for strength. "Bound or free" pairs opposites to mean everyone, whatever their state (1 Kings 14:10; 2 Kings 14:26); its exact sense is uncertain, perhaps "under restraint or at liberty".

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: As with Moses "the slave of the LORD", Literal keeps the hard sense of the word; Balanced and Readable say "servants".

decisions.choice: do justice for
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the sense of "judge" here; Literal keeps "judge".

source.text: וְאָמַ֖ר אֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ימוֹ צ֖וּר חָסָ֥יוּ בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will say, Where [are] their gods, [the] rock in which they sought refuge,

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say, 'Where [are] their gods, \q the rock in which they took refuge,
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say, 'Where are their gods, \q the rock they ran to for shelter,
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say, 'Where are their gods now? \q Where is the rock they ran to for safety?

decisions.choice: he will say: the LORD will say
decisions.reason: The speaker of verses 37-42 says "I, I am he" (verse 39), so he is God. The words can also be read "it will be said".

decisions.choice: the rock: the false god they trusted
decisions.reason: The song uses the word in mockery for the gods Israel turned to (verse 31).

decisions.choice: took refuge: trusted for protection
decisions.reason: The verb means to shelter in someone or something (Psalm 2:12; Ruth 2:12).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks from here to the end of verse 42
decisions.reason: These are God's words inside Moses' song.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר חֵ֤לֶב זְבָחֵ֨ימוֹ֙ יֹאכֵ֔לוּ יִשְׁתּ֖וּ יֵ֣ין נְסִיכָ֑ם יָק֨וּמוּ֙ וְיַעְזְרֻכֶ֔ם יְהִ֥י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם סִתְרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: who [the] fat of their sacrifices ate, drank [the] wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and let them help you; let it be over you a shelter.

en.L: who ate the fat of their sacrifices, \q [who] drank the wine of their drink offering? \q Let them rise up and help you; \q let it be a shelter over you.
en.B: who ate the fat of their sacrifices \q and drank their offerings of wine? \q Let them get up and help you! \q Let them be your shelter!
en.R: Those gods ate the fat of the animals the people sacrificed \q and drank the wine they poured out. \q Let those gods get up and help you! \q Let them protect you!

decisions.choice: the gods pictured as eating sacrifices and drinking offerings of wine
decisions.reason: The fat of an animal and wine poured out were offered to gods as food. The question mocks gods who received so much and could give nothing back (Psalm 50:13; Isaiah 46:1-7).

decisions.choice: drink offering: wine poured out as an offering
decisions.reason: Wine was poured out with sacrifices to Israel's God as well (Numbers 15:5-10).

decisions.choice: help you, over you: God turns to address the people
decisions.reason: The words are a challenge to Israel: let their gods save them now.

source.text: רְא֣וּ׀עַתָּ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י אֲנִי֙ ה֔וּא וְאֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּדִ֑י אֲנִ֧י אָמִ֣ית וַאֲחַיֶּ֗ה מָחַ֨צְתִּי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶרְפָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין מִיָּדִ֖י מַצִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: See now that I, I [am] he, and there is no god with me; I put to death and I make alive; I have wounded and I will heal, and there is none from my hand delivering.

en.L: See now that I, I [am] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, \q and [there is] no god beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q I put to death and I make alive; I have wounded, and I will heal, \q and [there is] no one who delivers from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.
en.B: See now that I, even I, am {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; \q there is no god beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I put to death and I bring to life; I wound and I heal, \q and no one can rescue from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.
en.R: See now that I am the one true God. \q There is no other god besides {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I put to death and I give life. I wound and I heal. \q No one can rescue anyone from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power.

decisions.choice: I, I am he: God alone is the God who acts
decisions.reason: The doubled "I" is emphatic. The same self-declaration is taken up in Isaiah 41:4; 43:10, 13; 48:12. The false gods of verses 37-38 are nothing; he is.

decisions.choice: with me: beside me, alongside me
decisions.reason: No other god shares his power (4:35, 39; Isaiah 45:5-6).

decisions.choice: death and life, wounding and healing are in his hands
decisions.reason: God both judges and restores (1 Samuel 2:6; Hosea 6:1). The healing points to verse 43.

decisions.choice: from my hand: from my power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, as in verse 36.

decisions.choice: I am the one true God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the emphatic "I, I am he" claims.

source.text: כִּֽי־אֶשָּׂ֥א אֶל־שָׁמַ֖יִם יָדִ֑י וְאָמַ֕רְתִּי חַ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י לְעֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For I lift up to heaven my hand, and I say, Living [am] I forever,

en.L: For I lift up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to heaven \q and say: as I live forever,
en.B: For I raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to heaven \q and swear: as surely as I live forever,
en.R: I raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand toward heaven and make this promise: \q As surely as I live forever,

decisions.choice: lift up my hand to heaven: take an oath
decisions.reason: Raising the hand was the gesture of swearing (Genesis 14:22; Exodus 6:8; Ezekiel 20:5).

decisions.choice: as I live: God swears by his own life
decisions.reason: There is no one greater to swear by, so God swears by himself (Numbers 14:21, 28; Hebrews 6:13). The oath's content follows in verses 41-42.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks for the oath
decisions.reason: The oath runs on into verses 41-42 as part of God's speech, so it is not set off with further quotation marks.

source.text: אִם־שַׁנּוֹתִי֙ בְּרַ֣ק חַרְבִּ֔י וְתֹאחֵ֥ז בְּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט יָדִ֑י אָשִׁ֤יב נָקָם֙ לְצָרָ֔י וְלִמְשַׂנְאַ֖י אֲשַׁלֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: if I sharpen [the] lightning of my sword, and takes hold on judgment my hand, I will return vengeance to my adversaries, and to those hating me I will repay.

en.L: when I sharpen {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flashing sword, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand takes hold of judgment, \q I will return vengeance on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} adversaries, \q and those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I will repay.
en.B: when I sharpen {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flashing sword \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand grasps judgment, \q I will take vengeance on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} foes \q and pay back those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: when I sharpen {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shining sword \q and take hold of it to judge, \q I will punish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies. \q I will pay back those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the lightning of my sword: my gleaming, flashing blade
decisions.reason: A polished sword flashes like lightning (Nahum 3:3; Ezekiel 21:15).

decisions.choice: when: the condition of the oath
decisions.reason: The word usually means "if"; after an oath it introduces what will surely happen.

decisions.choice: vengeance: just punishment, as in verse 35
decisions.reason: God punishes those who set themselves against him.

source.text: אַשְׁכִּ֤יר חִצַּי֙ מִדָּ֔ם וְחַרְבִּ֖י תֹּאכַ֣ל בָּשָׂ֑ר מִדַּ֤ם חָלָל֙ וְשִׁבְיָ֔ה מֵרֹ֖אשׁ פַּרְע֥וֹת אוֹיֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: I will make drunk my arrows from blood, and my sword will devour flesh, from [the] blood of [the] slain and [the] captive, from [the] head of [the] long-haired of [the] enemy.

en.L: I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrows drunk with blood, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will devour flesh, \q with the blood of the slain and the captives, \q from the heads of the long-haired leaders of the enemy.'
en.B: I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} arrows drunk with blood, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will eat flesh: \q the blood of the slain and the captives, \q the heads of the enemy's long-haired leaders.'
en.R: My arrows will drink their fill of blood, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will eat flesh: \q the blood of the dead and the captured, \q the heads of the enemy's leaders.'

decisions.choice: long-haired leaders: warriors with flowing hair, the enemy's chiefs
alternatives: the hairy head of the enemy
decisions.reason: The word means loose, flowing hair, perhaps of warriors under a vow (Judges 5:2; Numbers 6:5). Some take it to mean "leaders". The Greek translation reads "the heads of the rulers of the enemies".

decisions.choice: arrows drunk with blood, a sword that eats flesh: the slaughter of battle
decisions.reason: The same vivid pictures describe God's judgment in Isaiah 34:5-6 and Jeremiah 46:10.

decisions.choice: the single quotation mark closes God's speech
decisions.reason: God's words from verse 37 end here; verse 43 is the singer's closing call.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable gives the simpler sense and leaves out the long hair.

source.text: הַרְנִ֤ינוּ גוֹיִם֙ עַמּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י דַם־עֲבָדָ֖יו יִקּ֑וֹם וְנָקָם֙ יָשִׁ֣יב לְצָרָ֔יו וְכִפֶּ֥ר אַדְמָת֖וֹ עַמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Shout for joy, nations, his people, for [the] blood of his servants he will avenge, and vengeance he will return to his adversaries, and he will make atonement [for] his land, his people.

en.L: Shout for joy, nations, [with] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will avenge the blood of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will return vengeance on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} adversaries \q and make atonement for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."
en.B: Nations, shout for joy with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will avenge {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants' blood. \q He will repay {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} foes with vengeance \q and make atonement for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."
en.R: You nations, celebrate with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will punish those who killed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants. \q He will pay back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies \q and make atonement for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} land and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people."

decisions.choice: the shorter text of the standard Hebrew
alternatives: Rejoice, heavens, with him; bow down to him, all gods
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew has four lines. A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran has six, beginning "Rejoice, heavens, with him, and bow down to him, all gods" and adding "and he will repay those who hate him". The Greek translation is longer still, with lines calling the sons of God and the angels of God to worship him. Hebrews 1:6 quotes a line close to the Greek ("let all God's angels worship him"), and Romans 15:10 quotes "Rejoice, nations, with his people". This text follows the standard Hebrew. Reviewers check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: shout for joy, nations, with his people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "nations" and "his people" side by side with no word between them. It may mean "rejoice, nations, with his people" (as the Greek and Romans 15:10 have it), "nations, praise his people", or "rejoice, nations; rejoice, his people".

decisions.choice: make atonement for his land, his people: cleanse the land and people from the guilt of bloodshed
decisions.reason: Blood shed on the land defiles it, and atonement cleanses it (21:1-9; Numbers 35:33). The Qumran manuscript, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek read "the land of his people".

decisions.choice: he will avenge the blood of his servants: God will set right the wrong done to his people
decisions.reason: The song ends not with destruction but with God defending his people and cleansing his land (verses 35-36, 39).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: As in verse 36.

decisions.choice: the double quotation mark closes the song
decisions.reason: The song that opened at verse 1 ends here.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַשִּׁירָֽה־הַזֹּ֖את בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם ה֖וּא וְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ בִּן־נֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Moses and spoke all [the] words of the song the this in [the] ears of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.

en.L: And Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.
en.B: Moses, together with Joshua son of Nun, came and recited the whole song for the people to hear.
en.R: Moses and Joshua son of Nun came and spoke all the words of this song so that the people could hear them.

decisions.choice: Hoshea: Joshua's earlier name
decisions.reason: Hoshea was Joshua's name until Moses called him Joshua (Numbers 13:8, 16). Only here is the old name used after that. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation read "Joshua".

decisions.choice: in the ears of the people: so that the people heard
decisions.reason: Moses did what God told him: write the song and teach it to Israel (31:19, 22, 30).

decisions.choice: he and Joshua: Moses and his successor together
decisions.reason: Joshua had just been commissioned to lead the people after Moses (31:7-8, 14, 23).

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the name the reader knows; Literal keeps "Hoshea" as the Hebrew has it.

source.text: וַיְכַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֗ה לְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And finished Moses to speak all the words the these to all Israel,

en.L: And Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
en.B: When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
en.R: When Moses had finished saying all these words to all the people of Israel,

decisions.choice: all these words: the song, and with it the teaching Moses had given
decisions.reason: The words point back to the song just recited; the same phrase closes the writing of the law in 31:24.

decisions.choice: when ... had finished
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 46, so Balanced and Readable make this a time clause.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ שִׂ֣ימוּ לְבַבְכֶ֔ם לְכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מֵעִ֥יד בָּכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר תְּצַוֻּם֙ אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֣ר לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: and he said to them, Set your heart to all the words which I [am] warning you the day, that you command them [to] your children, to keep to do all [the] words of the law the this.

en.L: and he said to them, "Set your heart on all the words that I am testifying to you today, which you shall command your children, to be careful to do all the words of this law.
en.B: he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you today, so that you may command your children to be careful to do all the words of this law.
en.R: he said to them, "Think carefully about all the words I have warned you with today. Command your children to obey carefully every word of this teaching.

decisions.choice: set your heart on: give your whole attention to, take to heart
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought and will; to set it on something is to fix the mind on it.

decisions.choice: testifying: solemnly warning, bearing witness
decisions.reason: The verb is used for calling witnesses and for solemn warning (4:26; 30:19; 31:28). The song itself is to be a witness (31:19, 21).

decisions.choice: this law: the whole of Moses' teaching
decisions.reason: As at 1:5, the word means instruction, everything Moses taught, not only rules.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the word Literal and Balanced render "law".

decisions.choice: quotation marks open here and close at the end of verse 47
decisions.reason: Moses' words to the people are a quotation inside the narrative.

source.text: כִּ֠י לֹֽא־דָבָ֨ר רֵ֥ק הוּא֙ מִכֶּ֔ם כִּי־ה֖וּא חַיֵּיכֶ֑ם וּבַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה תַּאֲרִ֤יכוּ יָמִים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם עֹבְרִ֧ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For not a word empty [is] it from you, for it [is] your life, and by the word the this you will prolong days on the land which you [are] crossing the Jordan there to possess it.

en.L: For it [is] not an empty word for you, for it [is] your life; and by this word you will prolong [your] days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of [it]."
en.B: It is no empty word for you; it is your very life. By this word you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
en.R: These are not just empty words. They are your life! By obeying them you will live a long time in the land across the Jordan River that you are going to take."

decisions.choice: an empty word: a thing of no account, without effect
decisions.reason: The word means empty or worthless. The teaching is not a matter that can be set aside without consequence; compare 30:11-14, where the command is not too hard or far away.

decisions.choice: it is your life: obeying the teaching is the way of life
decisions.reason: Moses has set before Israel life and death (30:15-20; 8:3).

decisions.choice: prolong days: live long
decisions.reason: The same promise is attached to obedience in 4:40; 5:33; 11:9.

decisions.choice: by obeying them
decisions.reason: Readable says how the word gives long life: by being obeyed.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּעֶ֛צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses on [the] bone of the day the this, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses on that very day, saying,
en.B: On that very day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: That same day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: on the bone of this day: on that very day
decisions.reason: "Bone" here means the very substance of the day (Genesis 7:13; 17:23; Exodus 12:17). It is the day the song was taught.

decisions.choice: the LORD's word to Moses about his death
decisions.reason: God said the same in Numbers 27:12-14; now the time has come.

source.text: עֲלֵ֡ה אֶל־הַר֩ הָעֲבָרִ֨ים הַזֶּ֜ה הַר־נְב֗וֹ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֣י יְרֵח֑וֹ וּרְאֵה֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַאֲחֻזָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Go up to mountain the Abarim the this, Mount Nebo, which [is] in [the] land of Moab, which [is] on [the] face of Jericho, and see [the] land of Canaan which I [am] giving to [the] sons of Israel as a possession.

en.L: "Go up into this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which [is] in the land of Moab, which [is] opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel as a possession.
en.B: "Climb Mount Nebo here in the Abarim range, in the land of Moab, facing Jericho, and look out over the land of Canaan, which I am giving the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to possess.
en.R: "Climb Mount Nebo in the Abarim mountains. It is in the land of Moab, facing Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to be their own.

decisions.choice: the Abarim mountains and Mount Nebo
decisions.reason: The Abarim are the highlands of Moab east of the Dead Sea and the Jordan; Nebo is one of their peaks, from which the land west of the Jordan can be seen (Numbers 27:12; 33:47-48; 34:1).

decisions.choice: opposite Jericho: facing Jericho across the Jordan
decisions.reason: Jericho lay west of the river, in view of Nebo.

decisions.choice: possession: land held as a permanent property
decisions.reason: The word is used for land held by a family or people (Genesis 17:8; Leviticus 25:24).

decisions.choice: quotation marks open here and close at the end of verse 52
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to Moses are a quotation inside the narrative.

source.text: וּמֻ֗ת בָּהָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ עֹלֶ֣ה שָׁ֔מָּה וְהֵאָסֵ֖ף אֶל־עַמֶּ֑יךָ כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־מֵ֞ת אַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ בְּהֹ֣ר הָהָ֔ר וַיֵּאָ֖סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And die on the mountain which you [are] going up there, and be gathered to your people, just as died Aaron your brother on Hor the mountain and was gathered to his people,

en.L: And die on the mountain that you are going up, and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
en.B: On the mountain you climb you will die and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother, who died on Mount Hor, was gathered to his people,
en.R: You will die on the mountain you climb, and you will join your people who died before you. That is what happened to your brother Aaron, who died on Mount Hor and joined his people.

decisions.choice: die and be gathered: an announcement of what will happen
decisions.reason: The verbs are commands in form, but they declare what God has decided (Numbers 27:13).

decisions.choice: be gathered to your people: die and join your ancestors who have died
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of Abraham, Jacob and Aaron (Genesis 25:8; 49:33; Numbers 20:24, 26).

decisions.choice: Aaron's death on Mount Hor
decisions.reason: Aaron died on Mount Hor on the border of Edom (Numbers 20:22-29; 33:38-39).

decisions.choice: you will die
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the command into the announcement it is; Literal keeps the command.

source.text: עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר מְעַלְתֶּ֜ם בִּ֗י בְּתוֹךְ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּמֵֽי־מְרִיבַ֥ת קָדֵ֖שׁ מִדְבַּר־צִ֑ן עַ֣ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־קִדַּשְׁתֶּם֙ אוֹתִ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: because that you broke faith with me in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel at [the] waters of Meribah-kadesh, [the] wilderness of Zin, because that not you treated as holy me in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel,

en.L: because you broke faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, [in the] wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: because both of you broke faith with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, and because you did not treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: This is because you and Aaron were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in front of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at the waters of Meribah near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. You did not show them that I am holy.

decisions.choice: the waters of Meribah at Kadesh
decisions.reason: At Kadesh, when the people quarreled for lack of water, Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it (Numbers 20:1-13; 27:14). "Meribah" means "quarreling".

decisions.choice: broke faith: acted unfaithfully, betrayed trust
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a serious breach of loyalty toward God (Leviticus 5:15; 26:40).

decisions.choice: did not treat me as holy: did not honor God's holiness before the people
decisions.reason: By not trusting and obeying God's word they failed to show the people how holy he is (Numbers 20:12).

decisions.choice: you: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural; both brothers are meant (Numbers 20:12, 24).

decisions.choice: both of you; you and Aaron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "you" is plural.

records.literal_gloss: for from opposite you will see the land, and there you will not go, to the land which I [am] giving to [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: For from a distance you will see the land, but you will not go there, into the land that I am giving to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."
en.B: You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it, the land I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."
en.R: You will see the land from far away, but you will not go into the land that I am giving to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

decisions.choice: from a distance: from where you stand, facing it
decisions.reason: The word means in front of, opposite; Moses will see the land spread out before him (3:27; 34:1-4).

decisions.choice: you will not go there: Moses' exclusion from the land
decisions.reason: God had refused Moses' plea to cross over (1:37; 3:23-27). Chapter 34 tells how this was fulfilled.

decisions.choice: the quotation mark closes the LORD's words
decisions.reason: The LORD's speech that began in verse 49 ends here.
